title: Rise of the Authoritarian States
description: Italy, the USSR, and Germany, 1917–1938 — how three single-party states were built.

events.text: The Bolsheviks seize power in Russia
events.note: Anchor event: the starting point for the Soviet case study.

events.text: Benito Mussolini's March on Rome leads to his appointment as Prime Minister
events.note: Italy is the first of the three states to fall under single-party rule.

events.text: Vladimir Lenin dies, opening a succession struggle in the Soviet Union
events.note: Begins the power struggle that Stalin eventually wins.

events.text: Mussolini publicly claims responsibility for Fascist violence and declares a dictatorship
events.note: The point at which Fascist Italy stops pretending to be a normal parliamentary state.

events.text: Stalin launches the first Five-Year Plan in the Soviet Union
Adolf Hitler is appointed Chancellor of Germany
events.note: Bridges Topic 4 (Authoritarian States) and the Germany country study.

events.text: The German Reichstag passes the Enabling Act, letting Hitler's government rule by decree
events.note: The key legal step in the Nazi consolidation of power.

events.text: The Night of the Long Knives: Hitler purges the SA leadership and other rivals
events.note: Removes internal Nazi Party rivals and reassures the army.

events.text: Soviet official Sergei Kirov is assassinated in Leningrad
events.note: Used by Stalin as a pretext to launch the Great Terror.

events.text: Germany annexes Austria in the Anschluss
events.note: Marks the start of Nazi Germany's territorial expansion.
